title: Finite-quotient scheme products and their component topology
statement:
Let $G$ be a profinite group (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group), and $q\geq0$ an integer. Index by all open normal subgroups $N\triangleleft G$, with quotient maps for $M\subseteq N$. The canonical map
$$G\longrightarrow\varprojlim_NG/N$$
is a homeomorphism of topological groups; the quotient projections and their finite products generate the topology, and $G^q\simeq\varprojlim_N(G/N)^q$. Put $P=G^q$. For any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], its profinite test product $T[P]$ and constant-label sections are those of [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects, def-sfb-profinite-product-maps]. There is a canonical limit identification over $T$
$$T[P]\simeq\varprojlim_N\coprod_{(G/N)^q}T,$$
whose projection on the section of label $a\in P$ is inclusion into the summand labelled by its image in $(G/N)^q$. For any affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the inverse image of $W$ is canonically
$$\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_N A^{(G/N)^q})\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(P,A),$$
where $\operatorname{LC}(P,A)$ is the ring of locally constant functions with pointwise operations; the ring colimit identification is induced by precomposition with $P\to(G/N)^q$. These identifications commute with restriction to affine opens and induce a homeomorphism $|T[P]|\simeq|T|\times P$ over $|T|$, carrying constant-label sections to their indicated fibres. If $T$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], the fibres $|T|\times\{a\}$ are exactly the connected components and the projection to $P$ is an open quotient map. Consequently $\pi_0(|T[P]|)\simeq P$ for the quotient topology on connected components. These comparisons are natural under scheme morphisms and continuous homomorphisms of profinite groups, and include $q=0$. All objects and inverse limits obey [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Use Mathlib ProfiniteGrp.continuousMulEquivLimittoFiniteQuotientFunctor for the canonical group limit map. Composing its inducing map with the compatible-family subtype inclusion gives the topology generated by the quotient coordinates (the bundled and quotient topologies agree since both are discrete). For each coordinate of a compatible family of q-tuples use ProfiniteGrp.toLimit_surjective to obtain a group element; injectivity follows from ProfiniteGrp.toLimit_injective coordinatewise. The continuous resulting bijection from the compact finite power to the Hausdorff compatible-family subspace is a homeomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-compact-hausdorff-bijection]. Composing with its subtype inclusion proves the finite-power topology assertion. This argument includes q=0.

proof.text: Construct the actual profinite cone N ↦ (G/N)^q using quotient homomorphisms. Its universal lift is the inverse of the homeomorphism in step 1 applied to the cone coordinates. Each projection is onto by choosing a representative in each coordinate. The open normal subgroups form a nonempty cofiltered poset, since they have intersections and the top subgroup. This realizes the required small presentation.

proof.text: Apply the finite-stage and compatible-family constructions in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] and [lem-sfb-relative-profinite-test-labels]. The latter theorem supplies a colimiting finite family of sections normalized by base and absolute-test projection. Pullback extensionality identifies these with profiniteProductSection. Uniqueness of colimits gives profiniteProduct T Q ≅ ∐_Q T for finite Q, with the specified section formula. Naturality follows by checking each section. Apply the locally constant ring-limit lemma lc_limit from the former module, Spec preservation of limits, and base change in the over category. Connectedness of the cofiltered index lets Over.forget preserve this limit. Postcompose its cone with the finite-stage isomorphisms. The resulting projections form the required limiting scheme cone; the base and section equations follow from the pullback equations.

proof.text: For the specified ring cocone, apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-limit-function-factorization] to step 2: every locally constant A-valued function is a finite-stage pullback. Equality of two functions at a fixed stage is detected after precomposition by its surjective projection. Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' gives the universal property on underlying sets, and the forgetful functor from commutative rings reflects the filtered colimit. Thus the specified precomposition cocone is colimiting without restrictions on A.

proof.text: Construct the affine comparison directly by a ring pushout. The square from ULift ℤ to LC(P,ℤ) and A, with target LC(P,A), is a pushout: for maps into B, use LocallyConstant.liftPrimeSpectrum with the given coefficient map and the label map LocallyConstant.specMap of LC(P,ℤ)→B. The proved library lemmas specMap_liftPrimeSpectrum and ringHom_ext_of_specMap show both factorization identities and uniqueness; the label map is unchanged on restricting coefficients, by the evaluation-prime formula of [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum]. Applying Spec to this opposite pushout gives the actual pullback defining profiniteProduct, hence its canonical affine isomorphism. Its two projection equations give the base formula; pullback extensionality gives the evaluation-section equation. Maps from this affine product to a spectrum are determined by their restrictions along all constant-label sections, since the corresponding ring maps are determined by evaluating every locally constant function at every label. Test on these sections and use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to prove the finite-stage comparison.

proof.text: Pullback pasting and symmetry give the base-change isomorphism profiniteProduct U P ≅ U ×_T profiniteProduct T P for every U→T, with the required two projections. In particular the map above an affine open is an open immersion. Pair the global base map with the normalized label map of [lem-sfb-relative-profinite-test-labels]. On each affine chart, step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum] identify this pair with the product homeomorphism: constants recover the base prime, and restriction of coefficients preserves the label. Affine charts of T and their pullbacks cover source and target. Chart lifts prove bijectivity, and chartwise openness proves that the global pair is an open map, so the continuous bijection is a homeomorphism. No condition on overlaps is used. Its formula on sections and its affine evaluation-prime formula follow from the same projection and spectrum equations.

proof.text: Suppose $T$ is nonempty and connected in [def-weil-connected-scheme]. In $|T|\times P$, each slice $|T|\times\{a\}$ is homeomorphic to $|T|$ and is connected. Any connected subset has connected image in $P$, hence a singleton, since $P$ is totally disconnected. It is therefore contained in one slice. The slices are consequently precisely the maximal connected subsets, i.e. the connected components.

source.place: Tag 004S, definition-connected-components; direct separation argument for a product with a totally disconnected space.

proof.text: The projection $|T|\times P\to P$ is continuous and onto because $T$ is nonempty. It is open: each open set is a union of open rectangles, and the image of a rectangle $U\times V$ is $V$ if $U$ is nonempty and is empty otherwise. A continuous open surjection is a quotient map: if the inverse image of $V\subseteq P$ is open, its image is $V$, so $V$ is open. Step 8 identifies its fibres with the connected components. The resulting bijection $\pi_0(|T[P]|)\to P$ is a homeomorphism, because both topologies are characterized by openness of inverse images under this same projection.

source.place: Tag 004S, definition-connected-components, component quotient topology; openness checked on product rectangles.

proof.text: For arbitrary scheme maps and continuous label maps, the two pullback projections show naturality of the product base and absolute-test map. The evaluation-prime formula shows naturality of its label, hence of the global space comparison. For affine coefficient maps use the two projection equations of the affine pullback to prove naturality. For finite quotient maps b satisfying the stated factorization, regard b as a continuous map of the finite label spaces. Its composite with the quotient projection agrees with the group-induced map followed by the target quotient, by the assumed pointwise equation. Functoriality of the actual product maps and naturality of the finite coproduct comparison give projection_natural. All constructions include empty schemes, zero rings, and q=0 without additional hypotheses.
